commands.review_summary:
The branch pins Google’s Linux package-signing primary fingerprint in the Linux developer-tools script and Worker cloud-init browser bootstrap, adds mismatch coverage, scopes the Worker Chrome repository with signed-by, and documents the rotation policy.

Reproducibility: yes. for source-level reproduction: current main still downloads and trusts Google Chrome APT key material without a reviewed digest or fingerprint check in both affected paths. I did not run the privileged bootstrap locally during this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Security-sensitive fail-closed trust-anchor policy needs maintainer approval before merge, and the only mechanical cleanup is secondary to that decision.

target.title: fix: pin Google Linux signing key
target.body:
## Summary

- pin Google's published active Linux package-signing primary fingerprint in both managed Chrome bootstrap paths
- import downloaded keys in an isolated temporary GnuPG home and export only the approved primary plus its subkeys
- scope the Worker bootstrap to a dedicated Chrome keyring with `signed-by`
- fail before replacing a prior keyring or repository source when the primary fingerprint does not match
- document the intended primary/subkey rotation policy

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/719

## Maintainer decision required

Approve primary-fingerprint pinning as the rotation contract:

- approved primary: `EB4C1BFD4F042F6DDDCCEC917721F63BD38B4796`, currently listed as active on [Google's official Linux repository page](https://www.google.com/linuxrepositories/)
- signing-subkey rotations under that primary continue automatically
- a Google primary-key rotation fails closed and requires a reviewed fingerprint update plus fresh container proof
- no fallback accepts an unpinned or unexpected primary

Risk: a legitimate Google primary-key rotation temporarily blocks managed Chrome bootstrap until Crabbox reviews and updates the fingerprint. This is the intended fail-closed behavior.

## Verification

- `bash -n scripts/install-linux-developer-tools.sh`
- `shellcheck scripts/install-linux-developer-tools.sh`
- `node --test scripts/install-linux-developer-tools.test.js` (2 passed)
- `npm test --prefix worker -- test/bootstrap.test.ts` (17 passed)
- `npm test --prefix worker` (700 passed)
- Worker format, lint, typecheck, and build
- `scripts/check-docs.sh`
- autoreview: clean, no actionable findings
- `git diff --check`

### Disposable Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 proof

- live Google key selected the approved primary fingerprint
- live repository `apt-get update` succeeded
- installed `Google Chrome 150.0.7871.46`
- no Google key existed under `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d`
- Chrome's post-install repository remained scoped through its package-managed `Signed-By` keyring
- deliberate fingerprint mismatch exited nonzero, preserved the existing keyring and source, and removed temporary state

## Scope

NodeSource and Docker key policy remains unchanged and belongs to https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/687. No credentials, configuration, or provider behavior changes.
